node.title: Re: Using eval: $@ isn't returning the error I expect
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
I see a couple of issues here:

  • [pryrt] [id://11113200|pointed out] that you're using [doc://eval|eval BLOCK] syntax with a single string inside the block, that's basically like writing "use cPanelUserConfig;" in your code, i.e. it has no effect, and [doc://warnings] would have told you "Useless use of a constant ("use cPanelUserConfig;") in void context". Always [id://111088]!
  • [haj] [id://11113198|pointed out] that unless($@){use cPanelUserConfig} will always attempt to load the module. There's the [doc://if.pm] pragma, but in this case a simple eval "use cPanelUserConfig;" (that's an eval STRING) would be enough to either load the module or not.
  • The pattern of checking [doc://$@] after an [doc://eval] is unfortunately common, but it has issues: [id://1153468].

All in all, since it sounds like you only need to load the module or not, and not actually use any of its functions (?), I would have gone with: eval "use cPanelUserConfig; 1" or warn "Didn't load cPanelUserConfig: $@";.
